newsitem.title: POLAND: BRE, German ADIG to start mutual fund June.
newsitem.headline: BRE, German ADIG to start mutual fund June.

text.p: Poland's Bank Rozwoju Exportu SA (BRE) and Germany's Allgemeine Deutsche Investment GmbH (ADIG) will most likely begin selling joint mutual fund units in June 1997, the deputy president of BRE said on Tuesday.

"We plan to begin selling the units...in May or in June," Wojciech Kostrzewa told a news conference, but said that the start could be delayed until September if the fund did not receive a needed licence in advance.
ADIG, owned by Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Commerzbank AG, will have 40 percent of the company running the joint mutual funds and BRE will have 60 percent.
Kostrzewa said it was not yet decided whether the family of three funds, all with varying degree of risk, will be launched simultaneously or one at a time.
He said BRE and ADIG invested together 18 million German marks in the company, which hoped to get 10 percent market share of Poland's open-ended funds within five years.
